name: Government Issue
label: Dischord
lede: Almost a dozen members in nine years, a singer who outlasted all of them, and a band that kept changing its sound whether the hardcore kids liked it or not.

eras.title: They debuted as somebody else
eras.text: John Schroeder from Rockville took his stage name from a band called The Stab and built GI around it. Their first show went out under a fake name, their second got shut down by the cops, and by the end of 1981 they had a Dischord single and a Minor Threat member on bass.

years.h: John Schroeder becomes John Stabb and starts GI
years.p: [[John Stabb|898f9d0f-b024-45f4-b887-60aec4ba0eec]] recruits drummer Marc Alberstadt, guitarist John Barry and bassist Brian Gay. His stage name comes from The Stab, an earlier band Dischord says Stabb claimed to have joined.

years.h: GI's first show, billed as The Substitutes
years.p: At the two-day Unheard Music Festival at D.C. Space, with drummer Marc Alberstadt sick and guests filling in, Government Issue plays as The Substitutes. Police shut down its second show halfway through.

years.h: Legless Bull · Dischord No. 4
years.p: Ten songs, mixed by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] at Inner Ear. Steven Blush called it the best example of smartass suburban hardcore, and for a year GI were in the fight with [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]] for top band in town.

years.h: Brian Gay leaves for college, Brian Baker takes over bass
years.p: With Minor Threat on hiatus, [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] replaces Brian Gay on bass in GI. Baker said he joined the D.C. band he liked best that needed somebody.

years.h: Brian Baker goes to SNL, so Tom Lyle plays bass
years.p: Halloween 1981 is the night [[Fear|5e6512dd-160b-4512-a4b4-2c30fa894a08]] played Saturday Night Live with a D.C. crew slamming in the studio. Brian Baker goes, and [[Tom Lyle|b61fd366-0bcb-4aae-bea7-c0152ca67584]] covers bass at GI's show.
years.xp:
Fear's Saturday Night Live appearance came about through John Belushi, and a crew of DC punks including [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] went up to New York to be the audience. Baker was one of them, which left GI a bassist short on Halloween.

Lyle's night as a stand-in turned into the longest tenure in the band after Stabb's: bass, then guitar, and most of the music and cover art for the rest of the band's run.

years.h: Brian Baker's last GI show on bass: the 9:30 Club with T.S.O.L.
years.p: Baker's final show as Government Issue's bassist, before he moves over to guitar.

eras.title: Tom Lyle takes the wheel
eras.text: Members came and went so fast that the core became Stabb, Alberstadt and Tom Lyle, who switched to guitar, wrote most of the music and drew most of the covers. The songs got heavier and more like rock, and Dischord got its first Government Issue album.

years.h: John Barry moves to Bulgaria; Brian Baker switches to guitar
years.p: Guitarist John Barry leaves GI for Bulgaria. Brian Baker moves to guitar and Tom Lyle takes bass full time.

years.h: Make an Effort EP · Fountain of Youth
years.p: GI on record with Brian Baker on guitar and Tom Lyle on bass. Baker later said the band was better with John Barry but bigger with Baker in it.

years.h: Brian Baker goes back to Minor Threat
years.p: Baker rejoins Minor Threat, amicably, he said, once John Stabb calmed down. Tom Lyle moves to guitar and Mitch Parker comes in on bass.

years.h: Boycott Stabb: 20 songs cut, only the newest released
years.p: In November 1982 [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] produced GI at Inner Ear: 20 songs, older ones included. Dischord released only the newest as Boycott Stabb; the rest waited decades.
years.xp: The lineup was John Stabb, Tom Lyle, Mitch Parker and Marc Alberstadt. The outtakes finally surfaced on side B of Dischord's white-vinyl Complete Session.

years.h: Joyride · Fountain of Youth
years.p: Produced by Brian Baker, by then out of GI. Heavy, rocking, and a long way from Legless Bull.

years.h: Bassist Mike Fellows leaves GI for [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]]
years.p: Mike Fellows heads to Rites of Spring, one of the bands about to rewrite D.C. John Leonard takes over bass in GI.

eras.title: More than a hardcore band
eras.text: GI left Fountain of Youth for Mystic, recorded at CBGB, and started pulling in goth, pop and psychedelia. Founding drummer Marc Alberstadt left, former Minor Threat bassist Steve Hansgen arrived, and a planned joke about '70s prog turned into a real album.

years.h: The Fun Just Never Ends
years.p: Government Issue cut the basic tracks live at CBGB and finished them in a proper studio.

years.h: GI move to Mystic Records
years.p: Looking for more push, Government Issue leaves Fountain of Youth for Mystic, which puts out Give Us Stabb or Give Us Death and Live on Mystic.

years.h: Live at the CE Center, Philadelphia, February 23, 1985
yt: Live at the CE Center, Philadelphia, February 23, 1985

years.h: Marc Alberstadt and John Leonard walk out mid-album
years.p: Drummer Marc Alberstadt, the last founder besides John Stabb, quits during the sessions for the self-titled album, as does bassist John Leonard. Sean Saley takes the drums, and ex-Minor Threat bassist [[Steve Hansgen|cd469927-13a8-4d0b-8898-01c6856f5878]] joins.

years.h: Government Issue · Fountain of Youth
years.p: Tom Lyle says it started as a concept album mocking '70s prog; the concept was dropped but the interludes stayed. John Stabb is singing melodies now, with a lot of [[The Damned|77d21c13-846f-4f48-9546-873949eff6ae]] in them.

eras.title: Big tours, then the wall
eras.text: With J. Robbins on bass and Peter Moffett on drums, GI made its last two albums for Giant and toured the US and Europe hard. The early hardcore crowd didn't follow, and a van crash in England helped end it.

years.h: J. Robbins and Peter Moffett join GI
years.p: Sean Saley and Steve Hansgen are out after the self-titled record. With [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] on bass and Peter Moffett on drums, the last GI line-up is in place.

years.h: You · Giant Records
years.p: The first of two Giant albums; Giant also reissues GI's Fountain of Youth catalog. According to Wikipedia, it chronicled John Stabb's relationship with an underage girl.

years.cap: Released years later as Strange Wine: Live at CBGB
years.h: GI at CBGB, August 30, 1987
years.p: The New York show turns up in 2003 as the live album Strange Wine, with Tom Lyle remastering the tapes himself.

years.h: Full set at the Hung Jury Pub, 1987
yt: Full set at the Hung Jury Pub, 1987

years.h: Crash · Giant Records
years.p: GI's last studio album and its widest-ranging one. Steven Blush's verdict was that the fans still wanted Legless Bull.

q: We felt we were beating our heads against the wall.
years.h: A van crash in England, then GI calls it quits
years.p: A van accident on tour in England shatters drummer Peter Moffett's ankle. Back home, Government Issue breaks up.
years.xp:
J. Robbins has been clear that the crash was only part of it. After huge tours of the US and Europe, the four of them looked at where things stood and saw they each wanted something different.

By the end almost a dozen people had passed through, and John Stabb was the only original member left. Robbins went on to [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], and later reunited with Moffett in [[Burning Airlines|5ea472eb-5040-410c-b021-1e678276aed9]].

years.h: GI's last show: the 9:30 Club
years.p: The original run ends at the club where Brian Baker played his last GI bass show eight years earlier. J. Robbins remembered it as massive, ridiculous and fun.

eras.title: The archive opens, the band comes back to help
eras.text: Stabb went back to his given name and played in a string of D.C. bands while the catalog got collected and reissued. When he was assaulted in 2007, the old line-ups showed up to help.

years.h: Dr. Strange Records' Complete History Volume One
years.p: Dr. Strange Records starts collecting the Government Issue catalog. Volume Two follows in 2002.

years.h: Government Re-Issue plays a benefit for John Stabb
years.p: On July 17, five men assault John Stabb near his home and he needs extensive facial reconstruction surgery, Wikipedia reports. Two months later Stabb, Tom Lyle, Brian Baker and drummer William Knapp play a benefit for his medical bills and lost wages.
years.xp:
Help came from more than one direction. Part of the proceeds from the 2007 Riot Fest went to Stabb for his medical bills, and part to [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]], whose son had been diagnosed with spinal muscular atrophy.

The Government Re-Issue name was the joke; the line-up was not. Stabb, Lyle and Baker had last shared a stage in the early '80s.

years.h: GI's last line-up plays one more benefit
years.p: John Stabb, Tom Lyle, J. Robbins and Peter Moffett play D.C. as a benefit for local fan Steve 'Stereo Faith' McPherson.

eras.title: Legless Bull, one more time
eras.text: The original four got back together, liked it, and kept going. Stabb was on stages to the last months of his life.

years.h: GI at the Black Cat for Salad Days
years.p: Government Issue share the bill with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]] at D.C.'s Black Cat, a show supporting the Salad Days documentary, in which John Stabb appears.

q: Government Issue is a group again.
years.h: The Legless Bull line-up reunites at Damaged City
years.p: John Stabb, John Barry and Brian Gay reunite for D.C.'s Damaged City Festival, with Karl Hill on drums. Stabb said they had so much fun they'd keep it going.
years.xp: Thirty-three years after the first EP, the people who made it were back on a DC stage. It stuck: GI played Houston's Bad Ass Weekend in February 2015 and a five-date Southeast run that fall, including The Fest.

years.h: John Stabb's last show
years.p: Stabb's final performance, with History Repeated, the band he formed in 2008.

years.h: John Stabb, 1961–2016
years.p: John Schroeder died of stomach cancer at 54, in a hospice in Rockville, Maryland, where he grew up.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes a 112-day battle. On St. Patrick's Day that year he had married his longtime partner, Mina Devadas.

sources.title: Washington Post: John Stabb dies at 54
